column1: # COSMIC sources the Desktop image is built from, pinned to exact commits.
# The Buildroot package buildroot-external/package/cosmic builds them: it fetches
# each commit as a GitHub archive, applies board/desktop/cosmic-patches/<name>/*.patch,
# and runs the cargo arguments (a `-` means source-only: post-build.sh reads its data
# files). After changing a row, run scripts/cosmic-recipe.py to regenerate the
# The set is epoch-1.9.0 (cosmic-greeter 1.9.1) as of 2026-10-05. Note that an
# `epoch-*` tag is a Pop *release snapshot*, not a per-repo change: 10 of these
# rows already pointed at the commit epoch-1.9.0 tags (cosmic-idle and
# cosmic-randr have not changed since epoch-1.0.10), so only 16 rows actually
# libcosmic has no epoch tags and each component's own Cargo.lock pinned its own
# libcosmic commit (14 distinct ones). The build forces one rev across
# the whole set; the rev lives in scripts/cosmic-libcosmic.pin.
# The cargo-arguments column is a word list run as `cargo <args>`. It may be a
# `&&`-joined list of cargo commands when a component has to be built in more
# than one invocation — see cosmic-files below for why that is load-bearing.
# cosmic-osk: the on-screen keyboard. cosmic-session starts it at every login and
# the panel's OSK applet toggles it; until 26.10.23 it was not in this list, so the
# session logged "failed to start cosmic-osk" and the applet drove nothing.
# cosmic-files (the file manager) and cosmic-files-applet (the desktop) are ONE
# cargo workspace, and the applet depends on the app crate with `desktop-applet`.
# Building them in a single `--workspace` invocation lets cargo feature-unify
# `desktop-applet` onto the cosmic-files *app* binary too — the file manager then
# also creates the applet's full-screen Bottom-layer "desktop" surface and draws
# a second, interactive copy of the file view on the wallpaper (reproduced
# 2026-10-06 in QEMU; see CHANGELOG). Build the app and the applet as TWO
# invocations, app FIRST: the app binary must never be compiled with the feature.
# The cosmic package fails the build if the app binary carries it anyway.
